headline: Amendments to Students 503 attendance policy and 503-APP regulations, plus reports on chronic absenteeism and student conduct.
summary: The committee will review proposed changes to the attendance policy and its appendix regulations. It will also hear a school report card presentation, an update on chronic absenteeism, and a monthly conduct data report.

AGENDA 
 
MANCHESTER SCHOOL DISTRICT SAU #37 
 
COMMITTEE ON STUDENT CONDUCT 
 
October 21, 2026 5:00 p.m.  
Committee Members Hamer, Want, Stewart, Bergeron and St. John Aldermanic Chambers  
Alternates:  Committee Members Taylor and Smith City Hall (3 rd Floor) 
Student Representatives:  Madison Hanneman (MST) and Taegan 
Whyte (MST) 
 
 
1. Chair Hamer calls the meeting to order.  
 
2. The Clerk calls the roll.  
 
3. Public Forum 
 
4. Chair Hamer advises that the purpose of the public forum is to give the residents of Manchester 
the opportunity to address the committee on items of concerns affecting the community; each 
person will be given only one opportunity to speak; comments shall be limited to three minutes to 
allow all participants the opportunity to speak and any comments must be directed to the Chair. 
Any resident wishing to speak will come forward to the nearest microphone, clearly state their 
name and address when recognized and give their comments.  
 
5. Chair Hamer advises that if there is no one else present to speak and there are no other public 
comments that have been submitted, a motion would be in order to take all comments under 
advisement and to further receive and file any written documentation presented.  
 
 
6. Approval of the Minutes of the following meeting: September 16, 2026

5 full-day unexcused absences: 
• The administration or designee shall contact the parent(s)/guardian(s) in writing , in the family's 
preferred language, regarding the continued unexcused absences. 
• This correspondence shall provide the parent s wit h documentation outlining the unexcused 
absences. The written correspondence shall advise the parent that, should the absences continue 
one or more of the following shall take place: 
o A referral to the truant office r, court, diversion program , Office of Youth Services, 
Department of Health and Human Services 
o Filing of a truancy or educational neglect petition with the Court 
o Lass at efeeit Attendance-related academic review under Instruction 729 
• At this level the parent or student may appeal the unexcused absences 
Accountability and Reporting 
Teachers shall imp lement attendance and participation expectations and make timely referra ls; Principals 
shall monitor timeliness, consistency, data accuracy, and completion of required reviews; district 
administration shall review aggregate school-level results and direct corrective action; and the 
Superintendent shall report to the Board at least quarterly. Each report shall include, at minimum : 
ninth-grade first -semester attendance ; chronic -absence and unexcused-absence trends; time from 
trigger to first family contact; timely completion of required Attendance Plans; unresolved cases; 
attendance-related academic-cause codes; reasonable-alternative status; related failures and credit 
denials; principa l-review completion; school-level variation; and corrective actions. 
Nothing in these regulations shall be construed or administered to penalize a student who misses class 
or a required school event because of a school scheduling conflict. (N.H. Admin. Rule Ed 306.04(b)(1)(b))
